assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged line reads one documented configuration environment variable that selects where the app stores story data, falling back to the app's default local data location when unset. The resolved directory path is passed only to a fragment-listing helper used by a local HTTP route; it is never included in the route's response, embedded in any prompt or tool result, sent to a network destination, or persisted anywhere new. The route returns only a count and the matching fragment records for the requested story. No credential material, provider keys, or secrets are accessed, and no serialization of the wider environment occurs. This matches the project's documented filesystem-storage design, the bundled plugin template's manifest purpose, and the plugin system's stated capability to register API routes and fragment tools. The scanner signal is a generic environment-variable-read heuristic; the actual data flow shows a benign configuration lookup with no exposure.
assessments.layman_explanation: The flagged code asks the app for the folder where your stories are saved, which the app's own instructions say is set through a normal settings-style environment variable. It then uses that folder to list story fragments for the page it serves. Nothing is sent anywhere, no passwords or account keys are touched, and nothing about your system is shared beyond what the plugin is meant to show.
